Key takeaways

  • Anthropic does not publish a fixed message count for any plan. Limits are expressed as relative per-session multipliers (for example Pro = at least 5x Free) plus a rolling session window and a weekly cap. Every "N messages per day" figure you see elsewhere is unsourced.
  • The exact weekly quantity is confirmed to exist but is not published; the same is true for the exact per-session amount and any fixed Fable quota. Those cells stay marked "Not published" in the table below.
  • Plan prices as published: Free USD 0, Pro USD 20/month, Max 5x USD 100/month, Max 20x USD 200/month, Team Standard USD 25/seat/month, Team Premium USD 125/seat/month, Enterprise self-serve and sales-assisted USD 20/seat/month plus usage.
  • Context window (1M / 500K / 200K tokens) is a separate axis from the usage allowance, and is model- and surface-dependent.
  • Usage-based Enterprise plans carry no plan-level or seat-level usage limit; consumption is billed at API rates instead.

Usage limits vs length limits

Two different limits are easy to conflate when searching for "claude usage limits":

  • Usage limits cap how much you can use Claude over a period. Anthropic states them as relative multipliers (Pro = at least 5x Free per session; Max 5x = 5x Pro; Team Premium = 6.25x Pro) together with a rolling session window and a weekly cap. No plan has a published fixed message count. See the "Per-session relative usage", "Session reset window" and "Weekly limit quantity" columns above.
  • Length limits are about how much text fits in a single conversation: the context window. On paid plans this is model- and surface-dependent (1M / 500K / 200K tokens), which is a different axis from the usage allowance.

Both statements are limited to what Anthropic has published. Every unpublished cell in the table above is left as "Not published" and each published figure maps to S1–S9.

How Claude's limits are structured

  • Rolling session window. Paid plans reset usage on a rolling 5-hour session window rather than at a fixed clock time (see "Session reset window").
  • Weekly cap. A second limit applies per week and resets on a fixed time assigned to the account; Anthropic confirms the cap exists but does not publish its exact quantity.
  • Relative multipliers, not counts. Each tier is described relative to another tier, not in absolute messages (Pro = at least 5x Free; Max 5x = 5x Pro; Team Premium = 6.25x Pro).
  • Usage-based Enterprise. Enterprise self-serve and sales-assisted plans have no plan-level or seat-level usage limit; usage is billed by token consumption at API rates.

What Anthropic has not published

Across all eight plans the same fields are left unpublished, and the table keeps them that way rather than filling them with numbers taken from other sites:

  • Fixed message count — not published for any plan.
  • Exact weekly quantity — a weekly limit is confirmed, but its number is not given.
  • Exact per-session amount — expressed only as a multiplier relative to another tier.
  • Fable quota — billed through usage credits or API rates; no fixed quota is published.

This is why the page shows "Not published" instead of an estimate: a figure that no official page states cannot be traced to a source.

Frequently asked questions

Does Claude publish a fixed message limit?
No. The "Fixed message count" column is "Not published" for every plan in the table above; limits are relative multipliers plus time windows.
How long is the usage reset window?
Paid plans use a rolling 5-hour session window, and a weekly cap that resets on a fixed time assigned to the account (see the "Session reset window" and "Weekly reset rule" columns).
What are the current Claude plan prices?
As published: Free USD 0, Pro USD 20/month, Max 5x USD 100/month, Max 20x USD 200/month, Team Standard USD 25/seat/month, Team Premium USD 125/seat/month, Enterprise self-serve and sales-assisted USD 20/seat/month plus usage.
What context window do paid Claude plans have?
1M / 500K / 200K tokens depending on model and surface, per the "Context window published" column.
Which plans include Claude Code?
Every plan listed in the table records Claude Code access as "Yes" (see the "Claude Code access" column).
Why are some cells marked "Not published"?
Because no official Anthropic or Claude page states that figure. The table preserves the gap instead of substituting a number from a non-official source.

Who made this table, how, and why

  • Who: This reference table is published and maintained by usagecaptable.com as a public dataset of Claude plan usage limits.
  • How: Figures are transcribed only from official Anthropic and Claude pages (S1–S9). The page does not use its own testing, estimates, community posts or third-party blogs, and preserves every unpublished field as "Not published".
  • Why: So that people and automated agents have one citable place for these limits, with each figure mapped to an official source instead of repeated second-hand numbers.
